title: BSOD triggered when AlwaysOnTop module is enabled, especially around display sleep/reconfiguration
author: MickyLangello
summary: Strong crash-dump correlation exists, but the supplied archive was rejected and the author has not retested the current release or supplied fresh diagnostics.

status.label: Waiting on author diagnostics
status.detail: Needs-Author-Feedback is active after an invalid archive plus a request for a current-version retest and fresh diagnostics.

next_action.label: Wait for requested evidence
next_action.reason: The issue already asks for the decision-changing current-build retest and valid diagnostic archive.

judgment.rationale: The crash correlation is strong, but a kernel BSOD cannot be assigned to a PowerToys fix without the already-requested current-release reproduction and a valid fresh diagnostic archive.
evidence: The issue reports three 0x7F double-fault dumps with win32kbase PDEV recursion and no recurrence after disabling Always On Top.
The report was on PowerToys 0.100.2 and the triage comment requested a retest on 0.101.2362.0.
The attached report archive was rejected as invalid.
Needs-Author-Feedback remains active, with no later author reply, assignee, or linked fix.
judgment.recommended_action: Wait for current-version reproduction and a valid fresh diagnostic archive before routing a PowerToys root cause or design.

issue_context.summary: Display sleep/wake and monitor reconfiguration correlate with a kernel stack-recursion crash only while Always On Top is enabled, but current-build confirmation and a valid archive remain outstanding.
known_information: Three dumps reportedly show UNEXPECTED_KERNEL_MODE_TRAP 0x7F parameter 8 and win32kbase PDEV recursion.
The scenario uses two 1440p 180Hz DisplayPort monitors and repeated sleep, lock, wake, or monitor power cycling.
Disabling Always On Top stopped recurrence for the reporter while other PowerToys modules remained enabled.
Windhawk taskbar modules were installed, FancyZones was disabled, and the system was running Windows 11 24H2 build 26100.
The only upstream comment is the automated request for a valid bug report ZIP and a latest-stable retest.
inferences: Always On Top window-event activity may be a trigger, but user-mode hooks do not by themselves establish a kernel-mode root cause.
Display driver, shell modification, OS display-stack, and PowerToys event-hook interactions remain plausible until current diagnostics exist.
issue_context.analysis: The useful crash signature is already recorded, and the existing author request targets exactly what is missing. A new clickable request would duplicate that request rather than create a new maintainer action.
initial_investigation: Forced 2026-09-02 pass read the complete issue body, one triage comment, labels, empty assignee list, and timeline links; no linked work appeared.
Read src/modules/alwaysontop/AlwaysOnTop/AlwaysOnTop.cpp: Always On Top registers out-of-context WinEvent hooks for location, minimize, move/size, foreground, destroy, focus, and menu events.
No current-version author reply, valid diagnostic archive, assignee, duplicate, or fix PR is present.
